title: Colocated tenant-aware observability collectors for Dedicated & Private deployments
creator: Liam Chen
description:
Goal: build a colocated observability collector pattern for Dedicated and Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments that performs tenant-aware routing for traces/metrics/logs, enforces per-tenant scrubbing and residency controls, and minimizes tail latency impact on production inference paths. This ticket implements the runtime agent + collector pairing, buffering/backpressure strategy, mTLS auth and key rotation for cross-tenant-safe forwarding, and an operator-safe rollout path for customer-managed control planes.

Motivation: Customers running Redwood Dedicated/Private want parity of the hosted platform’s observability while retaining isolation and data residency. Current design options either require centralizing telemetry (violates residency) or shipping raw telemetry directly to cloud (unacceptable for many regulated customers). A colocated collector that batches, scrubs, and routes signals into controlled pipelines lets us provide the same dashboards/alerts with tenant guarantees.

Scope:
- Agent running co-located on the same host/instance as runtime pods (for on-prem appliance or VPC nodepool).
- Local collector that accepts agent streams over local loopback with mTLS and token attestation.
- Tenant-aware routing table: per-customer routing rules to destinations (Redwood-hosted ingestion, customer-owned endpoint, or S3 archive).
- Trace hook integration: automatic span enrichment for runtime service/span names, capture of KV cache IDs for correlation, and sampling controls that respect customer SLOs.
- Backpressure & durability: in-memory ring buffer + on-disk spillover + configurable max-retention for offline batch upload.
- Workflows: zero-downtime upgrades, automatic agent-collector version negotiation, and operator CLI for forced resync.

Non-goals: centralized multi-tenant store redesign, full-fledged SIEM integration (follow-up), replacing existing hosted ingestion for non-Dedicated customers.
comments: 2026-03-10 - Kickoff: scoped with Product and Security. Initial design doc linked; agreed to prefer local spill-to-disk over unbounded memory buffering to protect inference processes.
2026-03-11 - Decision: use gRPC over Unix domain socket for agent->collector; gRPC allows backpressure and flow control. Ops asked for a small protobuf v2 compatibility shim to handle version skew.

2026-03-11 - Tradeoff noted: aggressive batching reduces egress cost but increases tail latency for trace availability; we will expose batching config per-deployment with safe defaults (flush interval 200ms, max batch 500 spans).

2026-03-12 - Security review checkpoint: mTLS + token attestation accepted. Will integrate with customer KMS for collector keys and support HSM export for Private installs. Security requested a follow-up PRD for key rotation automation.

2026-03-12 - Implementation note: prototype collector implemented in Go using OpenTelemetry Collector SDK. Local disk spill implemented using LZ4 compressed chunks; found a minor bug with file handle leak during high churn - assigned to eng pair for patch.

2026-03-13 - Integration testing plan: run Collector locally against a Canary Dedicated cluster; generate synthetic load that mimics 95th pct token lengths to validate ring buffer behavior and CPU overhead. Also plan to exercise tenant scrub rules by injecting PII markers into logs.

2026-03-13 - PRs: initial collector core: github.com/redwood-inference/collector/pull/256; agent-side hook: github.com/redwood-inference/agent/pull/112; dashboard wiring: github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/410. QA assigned to @marie (integration tests) and @sanjay (load tests).
acceptance_criteria: Collector runs on Dedicated node and connects to local agent over Unix domain socket with mTLS and token attestation
Per-tenant routing rules configurable via control plane and applied by collector at runtime
Local buffering protects inference process under bursty telemetry load (no OOMs observed under 3x baseline traffic)
End-to-end traces appear in Dedicated dashboards with correct tenant tags and KV cache correlation IDs
Operator can perform zero-downtime collector upgrades with automatic version negotiation and fallback to previous binary on error
Automated tests for PII scrubbing rules and sample rate enforcement included in CI
notes: Follow-ups: SIEM export connector (ENG-13140), on-prem metrics retention policy UI (PM-558), advanced sampling policies tied to customer SLAs (ENG-13178).

Monitoring & alerts: create low-level alerts for collector disk-queue-saturation (>75%), agent-collector handshake failures (>1% of connects over 15m), and per-tenant high error-rate (>=5% trace drops).

Rollout plan: start with opt-in beta for three Dedicated customers, collect perf telemetry, then progressive enablement by workspace. Plan rollback window 72h after enablement with quick toggle in control plane.

Performance target: end-to-end additional p95 latency contribution from collector pipeline <= 15ms for synchronous trace forwarding; async flush paths may be larger but must not affect token serving latency.
